title: Benefits of Inpatient Addiction Treatment Centers

bodyHtml:
If you or someone near you is struggling with substance abuse or addiction, it might be time to consider inpatient addiction treatment centers. But what is an inpatient treatment center, and when is it the most appropriate solution?

What Is Inpatient Addiction Treatment?

Inpatient addiction treatment is one of two main types of addiction treatment; the other is outpatient treatment. Just like a hospital, inpatient treatment means you sleep at the facility. You stay there full-time during the course of your recovery. In contrast, outpatient treatment usually requires you to travel to therapy every week or a few times per week in and around your regular schedule.

When you use inpatient addiction treatment centers, you live at the facility for the duration of your treatment program. These programs are sometimes referred to as residential addiction treatment, and they give you a seamless transition between your detoxification and your long-term therapy.

Benefits of Inpatient Addiction Treatment

When you utilize inpatient programs at inpatient addiction treatment centers, you can reap physical, psychological, and emotional benefits. At the onset, you have fewer temptations. It will be much harder for you to get your hands on drugs or alcohol once you are inside the facility. Distractions are minimal, so you won’t have other responsibilities or stresses luring you back toward addiction. What’s more, the staff is available at all times to help you handle multiple substances or the effects of long-term addiction.

Physical Benefits

Inpatient programs start with a safe, medically supervised detox. Therapies can help change the way your brain responds to addiction, and your withdrawal symptoms can be managed during your most vulnerable period of rehab.

Psychological Benefits

Inpatient rehab gives you access to psychotherapy options, different treatments, and tights based on what you need most. You might want a facility that can help you address what is called dual diagnosis, meaning any underlying psychological disorders that you have an addiction to your substance abuse. These therapies can include motivational interviewing, cognitive behavioral therapy, and psychotherapy to treat things like depression, anxiety, or bipolar disorder.

The longer your inpatient program, the higher the likelihood of achieving long-term life skills and social skills that can help you avoid relapses. It’s not enough to simply do a detox program and move on. You have to learn how to manage your symptoms, how to take responsibility for your decisions, and how to exist in an environment that might be full of stress or triggers.

Emotional Benefits

There are emotional benefits to using inpatient treatment. Addiction requires medical treatment, but it also requires feeling safe, secure, and comfortable. Without arguments from family, stress about past events, screaming children, or work stress, you have the space to focus on yourself and your recovery, all while enjoying the emotional benefits of holistic therapy. Holistic therapy might include equine therapy or horse rides on the beach, yoga, meditation, nutrition, and fitness classes, all of which help you cultivate long-term skills to manage your stress, your temptations, and your addiction.

Is Inpatient Addiction Treatment Right For Me?

Using inpatient addiction treatment centers might be the right choice for you if:

  • You live in an environment where substance abuse is normalized, and it would be difficult to abstain while also attending your ongoing therapy.
  • You don’t have regular transportation where you live, so you would be unable to get to and from outpatient therapy.
  • You don’t have supportive friends and family and need an environment where you can focus exclusively on your needs rather than the needs of those around you.
  • You prefer privacy and a relaxing, comfortable environment where you have nothing else to focus on but your treatment.
  • You are free to leave work, school, or other responsibilities for between 30 days + 90 days, depending on your program.
